newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse dismisses talk of equity gains tax.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse dismisses talk of equity gains tax.

text.p: Athens stock exchange president Manolis Xanthakis on Monday dismissed press reports of a planned capital gains tax on equities saying they were unrealistic.

"To remove any doubt, we underline the position of the national economy ministry. Recent press reports regarding the imposition of taxes, especially on equities are not realistic," he said in a statement.

Financial weekly Isotimia reported on Saturday that Greece's national economy ministry was considering proposals to tax interest earned on state debt paper and capital gains from trading in shares, citing a 500 billion drachma shortfall in this year's budget.
Isotimia said the proposal by Greece's capital market's commission was "sitting in the drawers of national economy minister Yannos Papandoniou".
It quoted the alleged proposal as suggesting a uniform system of taxation on securities which should include taxes on interest, dividends, capital gains on equities and derivatives.
